[[Richmond, Virginia]] | former_school(s)= }} '''Edward Adam "Ed" Davis''' (born June 5, 1989 in [[Washington, D. C.]]) is a college basketball player who currently plays for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels]]. He played high school basketball at [[Benedictine High School (Richmond, Virginia)|Benedictine High School]] in [[Richmond, Virginia]]. He is the son of former [[NBA]] player [[Terry Davis]], who played 10 seasons (1989-2001) in the NBA with the [[Miami Heat]], [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[Denver Nuggets]] and [[Washington Wizards]].http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/davis_ed00.html Davis is considered by scouts as a dynamic scorer around the basket due to his smooth play and left-handed shot. Not only known for his offense, scouts praise his shot blocking and rebounding abilities.http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/player?recruitId=42906&season=2008&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fncb%2frecruiting%2ftracker%2fplayer%3frecruitId%3d42906%26season%3d2008 ==High School Career== Ed Davis spent his first two years of high school playing at [[Hanover High School (Mechanicsville, Virginia)]] before transferring to Benedictine High School. There, he led Benedectine to two state championships while averaging 22 points, 14 rebounds and 7 blocks as a senior. He accompanied current Tar Heel teammates [[Tyler Zeller]] and [[Larry Drew II]] in the [[McDonald's All-American Game]] and was selected to the Jordan Brand All-American Team. Davis and Zeller were also named to the 2008 Parade All-American Boy's Basketball Team.http://northcarolina.rivals.com/viewprospect.asp?pr_key=48045&Sport=2#ticker He was named Mr. Basketball of Virginia in 2008, which is given to Virginia's best high school basketball player. He also received recognition as co-player of the year in 2007. ==College career== ===Freshman Year=== Ed Davis played in every game during the 2008-2009 season, while starting in two of them. He averaged 6.7 points, 7.0 rebounds, and 18.8 minutes per game in his first season with the Tar Heels. Davis also led the team with 65 blocks with an average of 1.7 per game. In North Carolina's six wins during the [[2009 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament|2009 NCAA Basketball Tournament]], Davis averaged 8.2 points and 5.5 rebounds.http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2008-2009/teamcume.html In the [[2009 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament#Championship game – Michigan State vs. North Carolina|2009 NCAA Championship]], Davis came off the bench to score 11 points and grab a team high 8 rebounds helping the Tar Heels to a 89-72 win over [[Michigan State]].http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/basketball/ncaa/04/12/unc.davis.ap/index.html Davis was also named to the 2009 All-Freshman Team and was co-recipient of the team's Most Improved Player award.http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030909aab.html In April 2009, Davis announced he would return to the North Carolina after his freshman year instead of declaring for the [[NBA draft]]. He was widely projected to be a potential top 5 pick if he had opted to enter the draft.http://articles.latimes.com/2009/mar/22/sports/sp-heisler22 In February of 2010, he suffered a broken wrist in a loss to Duke, which effectively ended his season. He may still declare for the 2010 NBA draft. ====Statistics==== *Points:AVG 6.7 (Total:177) http://www.northcarolina.rivals.com/bviewplayer.asp?Team=UNC&Player=409863 *Field Goal Percentage:50.0% *Free Throw Percentage:60.6% *Rebounds:AVG 7.0 (Total:197) *Assists:AVG 0.7 *Blocks:AVG 1.7 *Steals:AVG 0.3 *Minutes:AVG 18.8 *Turnovers:AVG 1.1 ==Professional career== On April 12, 2010, Davis announced that he would forgo his final two seasons of collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2010 NBA Draft]], where he is expected to be a top 10 selection.{{cite news|url=http://acc.blogs.starnewsonline.com/13734/uncs-ed-davis-declares-for-the-nba-draft/|title=UNC’s Ed Davis declares for the NBA draft|date=April 12, 2010 |publisher=starnewsonline.com}} He has signed with [[sports agent]] [[Rob Pelinka]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsbusinessdaily.com/article/139218|title=Pelinka Signs Two Potential NBA Lottery Picks; Falk Inks Monroe|accessdate=2010-05-13|date=2010-05-11|publisher=[[Street & Smith]]|work=[[SportsBusiness Daily]]|author=Mullen, Liz}} ==Awards== *2009 ACC All-Freshman Team *2009 North Carolina's Most Improved Player(Jimmie Dempsey Award) *2008 McDonald's All-American Game Selection *2008 Jordan Brand All-American Team *2008 Parade All-American Boys Basketball Team *2008 Player of the Year Award (Mr. Basketball Award) *2007 Co-Player of the Year *2005-2008 Three-time All-Metro ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[http://realcollegebasketball.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=191%3Aed-davis-09-10-file&catid=49%3A09-10-players RealCollegeBasketball.com Profile] {{2009 North Carolina basketball}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Davis, Ed}} [[Category:African American basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball players]] [[Category:1987 births]] [[Category:Basketball players from Virginia]] [[Category:People from Washington, D.C.]] [[pl:Ed Davis]]
